post.description: Public. No bearer token. Anyone on the support site can open a ticket. Proof-of-work still applies (X-Debug: 1 skips it in development). The server joins first and last name, stores the email in lowercase, and sends an acknowledgment in Accept-Language. The email links to the site with the edit token. The 201 body is the only API response that includes that token. Later reads never return it. Keep the token: ticket ids are sequential, and the token is what proves this visitor owns the ticket.

parameters.description: Enabled dev mode (example skip PoW security)

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: Language of the response and the acknowledgment email

201.description: Ticket created and acknowledgment email sent. message.token is the visitor edit token.

500.description: Internal server error or email delivery failure

get.description: Staff only. Requires a bearer token. Visitors cannot list tickets. Returns 15 tickets per page, oldest first (created_at, then id). offset is how many rows to skip, not a page number: offset=0 is tickets 1-15, offset=15 is 16-30. There is no limit parameter. An empty page is { "message": [] }. The edit token is never included. data_updated is true when the visitor has appended text since the last staff reply.

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: Response language from the server

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Rows to skip. Page size is fixed at 15.

get.description: Same path for the visitor and for staff. Who is calling is decided by the query, not by a different URL. Visitor: pass token, the 64-character lowercase hex edit token from create or from the email link (http://localhost:5173/support/{ticket_id}?token=). Do not send a bearer token. The ticket is returned only when ticket_id and token match. A wrong token is 404, the same as a missing ticket, so the id alone does not confirm that a ticket exists. A token that is not exactly 64 lowercase hex characters is 400. Staff: omit token and send a bearer token. The ticket is loaded by id, including answer, status, assigned_to, and data_updated. The edit token is not in the JSON in either case.

parameters.description: Enabled dev mode (example skip PoW security)

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: Response language from the server

parameters.name: ticket_id
parameters.description: Public ticket id, YYMMDD-NNNNNN. 1 to 32 characters.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Visitor edit token. Required for an unauthenticated read. Omit it when calling as staff with a bearer token.

200.description: The ticket. Does not include the edit token.

400.description: Invalid ticket id, or a token that is not 64 lowercase hex characters

401.description: No token query and the bearer token is missing or invalid

404.description: Ticket not found, or the visitor token does not match this ticket

patch.description: Visitor only. No bearer token. Use this when support asked for missing details. The caller proves ownership with the edit token in the JSON body, not with a query parameter. The new text is appended to description after a blank line; the previous text stays. data_updated becomes true so staff can see that new information arrived. A wrong token is 404, the same as a missing ticket. This route does not change answer, status, or assigned_to.

parameters.description: Response language from the server

parameters.name: ticket_id
parameters.description: Public ticket id, YYMMDD-NNNNNN. 1 to 32 characters.

200.description: Description appended and data_updated set to true

400.description: Invalid ticket id, malformed token, validation error, or prohibited language

404.description: Ticket not found, or the token does not match this ticket

patch.description: Staff only. Requires a bearer token. The visitor cannot set the reply. The body is only the answer text; status is not accepted from the client. The server stores the answer, forces status to in_progress, sets assigned_to to the signed-in user, and sets data_updated to false. Status is never set to closed here. The reply is emailed to the address on the ticket, in Accept-Language, with a link back to the site that includes the visitor edit token. If that email fails after the ticket was saved, the response is 500 and the ticket is already updated.

who_blocked_uid.description: User UID who blocked the chat (0 if not blocked)

first_name.description: Given name. UTF-8, no control characters

last_name.description: Family name. UTF-8, no control characters

email.description: Address that receives the acknowledgment. Stored lowercased

description.example: The login page returns an error after I enter my email.

ticket_id.description: Public ticket id, YYMMDD and a 6-digit number

token.description: Visitor edit token, 64 lowercase hex characters. Returned only here. Pass it as ?token= to read the ticket, and in the body to append text.

name.description: First and last name joined by a space

description.description: Original text, plus any later visitor additions separated by a blank line

status.description: open on create. A staff reply sets in_progress. This API does not set closed.

assigned_to.description: User id of the staff member who answered. 0 when nobody is assigned.

answer.description: Latest staff reply. Empty until support answers.

data_updated.description: True after the visitor appends text. A staff reply sets it back to false.

token.description: Edit token from the create response or the email link

description.description: Text to append. It does not replace the existing description.

answer.description: Reply shown to the visitor and sent by email. Do not send status.
